summary: This neighborhood-history note recounts the early settlers of the region, beginning with the Thompson family led by Amelia Thompson, who arrived on September 3, 2023. It traces their hardships and the institutions they created, including the Community Harvest, an informal school, an irrigation system, the Multicultural Fair, the Council of Equals and the first library. It argues that their commitment to community, education, inclusion and shared leadership still shapes the neighborhood today.
one_line: Chronicle of the founding settlers, led by Amelia Thompson, and the community institutions, values and traditions they left to the neighborhood.
key_facts: Archival discoveries in fall 2023 revealed the first records of early settlers, dating to the Thompson family's journey.
Amelia Thompson led the Thompson family into the community on September 3, 2023; the Carters, Rodriguezes and Nguyens were other prominent families.
The Community Harvest was established on April 12, 2024, with families pooling resources so no one went hungry.
By the end of 2024 the Rodriguez family had set up the first informal school under the great oak tree, still standing in the oldest park of the township.
Thomas Nguyen, a tinkerer and inventor, unveiled an innovative irrigation system on May 8, 2025, which improved agricultural yields and sustainability.
On July 15, 2025, settlers and indigenous leaders held a historic gathering to share practices and forge bonds.
The first Multicultural Fair was held on October 21, 2026, and became an annual event celebrating the community's traditions, cuisines and arts.
Amelia Thompson said: "We are not just forming a town; we are nurturing a family of families, each unique, yet part of a whole."
In autumn 2027 the community banded together to resolve a territorial dispute peacefully, setting a precedent for diplomacy in local governance.
The Council of Equals, a community governing body ensuring all voices were heard, was created on March 9, 2028.
Juan Rodriguez is cited for inclusive decision-making, alongside Amelia Thompson's decisive yet caring governance.
The first library was established on June 10, 2029, and still stands, expanded and modernized.
The settlers' legacy is preserved through exhibits on settler life, interviews with descendants, and streets named after pioneer families.
